Base directory for this skill: <PLUGIN>\skills\wiki-maintainer

# Maintain content and perform requested app actions

Repair the requested knowledge or navigation while preserving its evidence and
other writers' work. A report alone does not authorize edits; a search answer does
not authorize filing. Pure filesystem maintenance needs no running app.

## Workflow

1. Read [access](references/access.md), resolve the known vault and absolute
   installed helpers, and open its applicable instructions. Select the requested
   action below; use [wiki-setup](../wiki-setup/SKILL.md) for report-only work.
2. Inspect the exact pages, current evidence and requested scope. Read
   [evidence](references/evidence.md) before factual changes and
   [identity and relationships](references/efficacy.md) before concept/navigation
   changes. Use the relevant direct setup check to establish the baseline.
3. Before a content or pipeline-state write, read
   [operation completion](references/operations.md), open or reuse the owned
   operation and retain the exact-path ledger. Native actions use the guarded
   adapter; a UI-only action does not require a content operation.
4. Make only justified changes. Preserve raw bodies, restrictions and factual
   review dates on mechanical edits. If support is missing or the intended change
   is uncertain, report the concrete remaining decision instead of inventing it.
5. Recheck the requested effect and [validate the changed paths](../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).
   Refresh affected owned catalogs, log once, close the scoped operation, sync and
   verify publication unless the user holds it. Report actual results and blockers.

## Modes and examples

- **Integrity repair:** read [repair](references/repair.md).
  Request: “Fix this broken citation.” Action: read the citing claim and exact
  source, repair its path within scope, compare issue IDs with the
  [health check](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog).
  Result: a verified citation repair and scoped publication, with unresolved IDs named.
- **Factual correction:** read [factual maintenance](references/lint.md).
  Request: “Correct the unsupported quotation on this page.” Action: inspect the
  [lint finding](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#content-lint-report) and raw passage,
  correct or mark the claim, then record the reviewed disposition. Result: supported
  text and an honest factual-review date, without changing the raw clipping.
- **Relationships and navigation:** read [relink](references/relink.md).
  Request: “Connect queue ordering to retry budgets.” Action: read both pages,
  accept only an explained relationship and update the relevant task map.
  Result: a useful navigational link with its limits, not an unsupported causal claim.
- **Triage:** read [triage](references/triage.md).
  Request: “Show the capture issues from this research run.” Action: present the
  queue's token-bearing link and topic summary. Result: the user can disposition
  the issues; opening the queue does not apply re-clips or quarantine. When asked
  to apply selected dispositions, act on those selections, validate affected
  content and complete the owned operation.
- **Authorized synthesis filing:** read [synthesis filing](references/synthesis-filing.md).
  Request: “File this cited answer as a synthesis.” Action: verify its provenance,
  reuse or create the proper synthesis and complete a **query** operation.
  Result: a sourced, validated, published page. Original project prose routes to
  [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).
- **Native action:** read [Obsidian actions](references/obsidian-cli.md).
  Request: “Open the Beacon architecture note in Obsidian.” Action: invoke the
  guarded helper with the exact note path. Result: the requested app action, or a
  specific unavailable-action report using [app diagnostics](../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md).
  A filesystem read is never reported as a successful UI action.

## Best practices

Compare resolved, remaining and new issue IDs rather than chasing a score. A
clean graph is not factual verification. Keep checks bounded to the task; skip
empty-vault or unchanged-wiki semantic sweeps. Distinguish preview from apply,
and inspect the target after an uncertain native mutation before retrying.

## Advanced references

Load [repair recipes and the hash-join contract](references/maintenance.md) only
for the indicated repair; [workflow overview](references/workflows.md) only to
compare roles. Required check procedures are directly available in
[checks](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md), [validation](../wiki-setup/references/validation.md)
and [operation recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md).
Removal retains separate approval boundaries in [wiki-purge](../wiki-purge/SKILL.md).

## Done

The requested effects are verified, remaining issues and coverage limits are
stated, and every owned content mutation is validated and accounted for through
publication or an explicit hold/local-only/blocker. Preview-only work has no
content operation, log, commit or refresh.

1	# Evidence and editorial policy
2	
3	## Page schema and dates
4	
5	Wiki frontmatter declares `type` (source/entity/concept/synthesis/authored),
6	`created`, `updated`, `reviewed`, `status` (stub/draft/maintained), `sources` and
7	honest `ai-generated` authorship. Follow the vault's schema; missing `reviewed`
8	means unverified, never substitute `updated`. Keep three dates distinct:
9	`updated` means edited, `reviewed` means claims checked against evidence or current
10	project behavior, and index freshness means indexed content matches the files.
11	Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.
12	
13	Use exact citation paths and `[[wikilinks]]`; `![[embeds]]` are transclusion, not
14	relationship edges. Write unwrapped logical lines and never split a wikilink over
15	a line break. Use [identity and relationships](efficacy.md) for concept reuse and
16	explained links. Original documentation follows
17	[authoring](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md).
18	
19	## Non-negotiable guardrails
20	1. **`raw/` bodies are immutable.** Read raw sources; never edit their content —
21	   it is the evidence every wiki page cites. Frontmatter is pipeline state and
22	   may be updated by wiki-master tooling only.
23	   Only clipping tools create raw evidence; never move it to record ingestion
24	   state. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it.
25	2. **Provenance on every claim.** Each wiki page you write carries `sources: ["[[...]]"]`
26	   linking back to the `raw/` notes it derives from, plus `ai-generated: true`.
27	   **Exception: `wiki/authored/`** — original content with no `raw/` counterpart
28	   (advisory documentation, policy, house style) declares this explicitly via
29	   `sources: []`, never by omission. `ai-generated` still records actual
30	   authorship (`true` if you drafted it, `false` if the human did) — the
31	   disclosure is about provenance, not about who wrote the words.
32	3. **Cite when you answer.** Query answers reference the pages/sources they rest on.
33	4. **Flag, don't invent.** If sources contradict or are silent, say so — never
34	   paper over a gap with plausible text.
35	5. **Clippings win.** Briefs, discovery summaries, corrections files, and your
36	   own memory of a source are *claims, not authority*: verify every quote,
37	   figure, and attribution against the clipping in `raw/` before it lands on a
38	   page, and when they disagree the clipping prevails — including when the
39	   instruction is the user's. Every layer between the source and the page is a
40	   lossy compressor whose errors read exactly like facts; authority flows
41	   outward from the one artifact that cannot drift.
42	   Scope edges, which matter as much as the rule:
43	   - It guarantees **fidelity, not truth** — a faithful clipping of a wrong page
44	     is still wrong; quality tiers and cross-clipping corroboration handle
45	     credibility.
46	   - A **degraded capture** (bad OCR, partial extraction) wins as evidence of
47	     what the vault *holds*, not of what the author typed — don't trust it at
48	     character level.
49	   - A clipping's **silence proves "not supported here," never "false"** —
50	     record unsourced claims as unsourced (visibly, on the page) rather than
51	     asserting or deleting them. The vault cannot cite what it does not hold.
52	
53	## Reddit and Medium
54	
55	Reddit posts and comments, and articles on medium.com or its subdomains, are
56	eligible sources. Keep their material in separate labeled sections in every
57	derived page and query answer: `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` for Reddit
58	and `## Medium articles` for Medium. Put platform-derived claims, quotes,
59	reported experiences and any inference that relies on them in the corresponding
60	section; do not blend the two platforms together or with higher-quality evidence.
61	This applies to source summaries, concepts, entities and syntheses, including
62	material reused through another wiki page. Even a summary of a single platform
63	source needs its heading. Raw clippings retain the captured content without rewriting.
64	
65	Attribute statements to their authors and cite the captured evidence. For Reddit,
66	do not turn a few comments into consensus, prevalence or established facts.
67	Disclose missing comments or reply context when the capture is incomplete;
68	do not claim a full thread was captured without verifying it. Upvotes do not
69	establish credibility.
70	
71	Keep Reddit and Medium citations and dependent conclusions out of the main factual
72	sections, opening summary and recommendations. A fact independently supported
73	by higher-quality evidence may appear there with those independent citations;
74	any platform comparison stays in its labeled section. Retain all provenance in
75	`sources:` frontmatter. Assess individual sources using the existing credibility
76	rubric; allowing capture does not automatically upgrade their credibility.
77	Official platform documentation and policy pages outside discussion threads or
78	Medium articles do not require these labels.
79	
80	## Style: viewpoints whole, conclusions after, breadcrumbs always
81	Narrative is licensed; dismissal is not. Three house rules govern every page:
82	
83	1. **Opposing viewpoints appear in their entirety** — in their own strongest
84	   terms, attributed to their holders — before any conclusion engages them.
85	   A viewpoint the page ends up arguing against gets the same care as one it
86	   endorses; weight follows the evidence the vault holds, and no viewpoint is
87	   waved off by tone (loaded verbs, scare quotes, "supposedly"). When sources
88	   conflict, keep the claims separate and attributed — never resolve them into
89	   one synthesized voice that erases the disagreement.
90	2. **Viewpoints first, conclusions after — and conclusions declare themselves.**
91	   Every analytic sentence is one of: *inherited* (a source says it — cite it),
92	   *extended* (built on a source — cite it, mark what's added), or *original*
93	   (the wiki's own inference — say so explicitly, never state it in the
94	   page's neutral voice). Joining source A to source B to imply C is an
95	   *original* claim even when A and B are both cited.
96	3. **The breadcrumb trail is non-negotiable.** Every viewpoint and every
97	   conclusion must be walkable back to `raw/`: `sources:` frontmatter, inline
98	   `[[wikilinks]]` to the source pages, and quotes verified per guardrail #5.
99	   A conclusion whose trail dead-ends is a defect, however good it reads.
100	
101	Per-type licenses (neutrality is a property of a page type, not of the vault):
102	- `raw/` — fidelity only; the evidence layer (guardrail #1, #5).
103	- `wiki/entities/` — **describe and only describe.** Convert opinions to
104	  attributed facts about who holds them; convert evaluations to the measurable
105	  facts beneath them. When tempted to interpret, link to a concept or
106	  synthesis instead.
107	- `wiki/concepts/` — claims with grounding. Assertive titles are allowed; the
108	  title's pressure is the point, and the body must support the claim under
109	  rules 1–3.
110	- `wiki/syntheses/` — the licensed narrative layer: weigh, judge, conclude —
111	  bounded by rules 1–3, and labeled as the wiki's synthesis.
112	- `wiki/authored/` — the vault's own first-party voice: advisory documentation,
113	  policy, house style, or other original work with no `raw/` evidence behind it
114	  by design. Same full narrative license as syntheses; state recommendations
115	  directly. Rule 3 (breadcrumb to `raw/`) does not apply — there is deliberately
116	  nothing to trail, declared via `sources: []` rather than left silent.
117	
118	Clippings carry `quality: high|medium|low`, an AI credibility rating. Treat low-quality sources with extra skepticism during ingestion; lint may flag claims supported only by low-quality provenance. Capture fidelity and source credibility are separate judgments.
119	
120	`citation-status: quarantined` is an explicit do-not-cite restriction, independent of credibility and character fidelity. Do not use that capture as supporting evidence or repeat dependent claims without independent support. Citing pages may carry `citation-status: restricted` and a warning identifying the affected evidence. ## Page schema and dates

Wiki frontmatter declares `type` (source/entity/concept/synthesis/authored),
`created`, `updated`, `reviewed`, `status` (stub/draft/maintained), `sources` and
honest `ai-generated` authorship. Follow the vault's schema; missing `reviewed`
means unverified, never substitute `updated`. Keep three dates distinct:
`updated` means edited, `reviewed` means claims checked against evidence or current
project behavior, and index freshness means indexed content matches the files.
Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.

Use exact citation paths and `[[wikilinks]]`; `![[embeds]]` are transclusion, not
relationship edges. Write unwrapped logical lines and never split a wikilink over
a line break. Use [identity and relationships](efficacy.md) for concept reuse and
explained links. Original documentation follows
[authoring](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md).

## Non-negotiable guardrails
1. **`raw/` bodies are immutable.** Read raw sources; never edit their content —
   it is the evidence every wiki page cites. Frontmatter is pipeline state and
   may be updated by wiki-master tooling only.
   Only clipping tools create raw evidence; never move it to record ingestion
   state. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it.
2. **Provenance on every claim.** Each wiki page you write carries `sources: ["[[...]]"]`
   linking back to the `raw/` notes it derives from, plus `ai-generated: true`.
   **Exception: `wiki/authored/`** — original content with no `raw/` counterpart
   (advisory documentation, policy, house style) declares this explicitly via
   `sources: []`, never by omission. `ai-generated` still records actual
   authorship (`true` if you drafted it, `false` if the human did) — the
   disclosure is about provenance, not about who wrote the words.
3. **Cite when you answer.** Query answers reference the pages/sources they rest on.
4. **Flag, don't invent.** If sources contradict or are silent, say so — never
   paper over a gap with plausible text.
5. **Clippings win.** Briefs, discovery summaries, corrections files, and your
   own memory of a source are *claims, not authority*: verify every quote,
   figure, and attribution against the clipping in `raw/` before it lands on a
   page, and when they disagree the clipping prevails — including when the
   instruction is the user's. Every layer between the source and the page is a
   lossy compressor whose errors read exactly like facts; authority flows
   outward from the one artifact that cannot drift.
   Scope edges, which matter as much as the rule:
   - It guarantees **fidelity, not truth** — a faithful clipping of a wrong page
     is still wrong; quality tiers and cross-clipping corroboration handle
     credibility.
   - A **degraded capture** (bad OCR, partial extraction) wins as evidence of
     what the vault *holds*, not of what the author typed — don't trust it at
     character level.
   - A clipping's **silence proves "not supported here," never "false"** —
     record unsourced claims as unsourced (visibly, on the page) rather than
     asserting or deleting them. The vault cannot cite what it does not hold.

Reddit posts and comments, and articles on medium.com or its subdomains, are
eligible sources. Keep their material in separate labeled sections in every
derived page and query answer: `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` for Reddit
and `## Medium articles` for Medium. Put platform-derived claims, quotes,
reported experiences and any inference that relies on them in the corresponding
section; do not blend the two platforms together or with higher-quality evidence.

material reused through another wiki page. Even a summary of a single platform
source needs its heading. Raw clippings retain the captured content without rewriting.

do not turn a few comments into consensus, prevalence or established facts.
Disclose missing comments or reply context when the capture is incomplete;
do not claim a full thread was captured without verifying it. Upvotes do not
establish credibility.

Keep Reddit and Medium citations and dependent conclusions out of the main factual
sections, opening summary and recommendations. A fact independently supported
by higher-quality evidence may appear there with those independent citations;
any platform comparison stays in its labeled section. Retain all provenance in
`sources:` frontmatter. Assess individual sources using the existing credibility
rubric; allowing capture does not automatically upgrade their credibility.

  moved (by path and by `source-hash`) and which source URLs were declined. Git-tracked, so a
  removal reaches every machine; dot-prefixed, so no search, metric or graph walk ever sees it.
  Never emptied automatically — a purge is reversible, and that is what makes it safe to run.

  clipping they summarize; this is the content key the ingest-backlog metric joins on.

  at most for a sub-project) and `kind` (`overview|architecture|reference|guide|

Concepts may carry `aliases: ["equivalent name"]` and a one-sentence `scope:`.

changes preserve `reviewed`; missing review means unverified. Index freshness

complementary topics and evidence; generated project catalogs are separate from
curated task maps. See `_templates/concept-note.md` and `_templates/task-map.md`.

operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. Obsidian Git stays installed for its
